site.name: Demo point C
site.locationHint: Lower-lying terrain about 32 km from the centre of Shackleton crater
site.description: Demonstration point in lower-lying terrain (below the 1737.4 km reference sphere) about 32 km from the centre of Shackleton crater, with surrounding relief that obstructs much of the horizon. Chosen for this prototype to contrast with the two elevated points. Not a NASA landing site; not selected, approved or recommended.
site.frameNote: Horizons reports the observer frame as 'MEAN_ME (high precision)' (ephemeris source DE441). The LOLA polar DEM is stated by its producer to be in the MOON_ME frame of JPL DE421. The residual difference between these two ME realisations was not quantified in this prototype; it is assumed (unchecked) to be small compared with the stated terrain-horizon uncertainty.
siteChecks: Inside valid LOLA coverage of LDEM_80S_40MPP_ADJ.TIF: bilinear surface height -376.6 m above the 1737.4 km sphere (all four neighbouring 40 m pixels valid).
Local slope from the DEM (central differences over +-40 m): 4.8 deg.
Terrain horizon over 720 azimuths: min -0.47 deg, max 9.58 deg, median 1.35 deg; horizon-defining terrain between 0.24 and 135.9 km.
Search completeness: 720 of 720 azimuths proven complete (no terrain up to the DEM maximum 7027 m could rise above the found horizon beyond the stopping distance); 0 azimuths flagged coverageLimited.
Resolution sensitivity: same algorithm on a 2x2-averaged 80 m grid differs by RMS 0.020 deg, max 0.125 deg.
Neighbourhood (+-1 km square of 40 m pixels): highest pixel -266.9 m at 1413 m from the point, lowest -430.6 m; the point is 109.7 m below the local high; 0 nodata pixels.
Ground distance from the centre of Shackleton crater (-89.67, 129.8 E; bowl location verified in the DEM by pipeline/tests/test_dem_real.py): 32.0 km.
LOLA height-error map (LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ_ERR.TIF): 0.1 m at the point; propagated to the horizon points gives RMS 0.010 deg.
Independent PDS LOLA GDR LDEM_75S_240M (heights relative to 1737.4 km per its label): -375.4 m at the point vs -376.6 m from the 40 m DEM (240 m smoothing).

ephemeris.corrections: Airless apparent topocentric direction of the body centre (Horizons quantity 4: light-time, gravitational light deflection, stellar aberration; no refraction). Azimuth clockwise from north through east; elevation above the plane perpendicular to the local radial zenith of the 1737.4 km sphere.

geometric.label: Geometric reference horizon (no terrain)
assumptions: Horizon is the local horizontal plane (elevation 0 deg) in every azimuth.
No terrain, no horizon dip and no lunar-curvature dip are modelled.
Body-centre direction only; a body whose centre is below 0 deg may still be partly above it.

terrain.label: Terrain horizon from LOLA elevation data
terrain.curvatureModel: Exact spherical geometry: samples placed along the great circle at ground (arc) distance d on the 1737.4 km sphere, terrain point radius 1737400 m + DEM height, observer radius 1737400 m + surface height + 2 m, elevation angle measured from the observer's local horizontal plane (perpendicular to the radial zenith). No d^2/2R approximation.

dem.projection: South polar stereographic on a 1737400 m sphere, natural origin latitude -90, scale factor 1 at the pole, central meridian 0 (x = r sin lon, y = r cos lon), PixelIsArea, upper-left corner (-304000, 304000) m, 40 m pixels (GeoTIFF GeoKeys)
dem.scaling: float32 metres used as stored: no scale/offset in the GeoTIFF metadata; GDAL_NODATA = NaN treated as missing; bilinear interpolation is NaN if any of the 4 neighbours is NaN or off-raster

assumptions: Azimuth bins every 0.5 deg starting at 0 deg, clockwise from local north (same sense as Horizons); horizon elevation is the maximum elevation angle of DEM terrain along each azimuth.

Ray samples every 20 m (half a pixel) from 80 m to at most 300 km; a ray stops at the first nodata/off-raster sample and is flagged coverageLimited if that happens before the search is proven complete.
Proven-complete criterion: the ray stops once terrain at the DEM's global maximum height (7027 m) could no longer reach the running maximum elevation angle at any farther distance.

Terrain closer than 80 m (2 pixels) is not sampled: the 40 m DEM cannot resolve metre-scale relief around a 2 m mast; boulders, small craters and local slope breaks inside a pixel are not represented.
The 80 m comparison horizon re-derives the surface height from the 80 m grid as well, so the resolution term includes the DEM's uncertainty in the observer's own height (deliberate).

uncertaintyDeg = max(0.05, RMS of the 40 m vs 80 m horizon difference combined in quadrature with the producer's height error propagated to the horizon points), rounded up to 0.01 deg. It is an estimate, not a validated error bound.
Frame: LOLA MOON_ME (DE421) treated as identical to Horizons MEAN_ME; residual not quantified.
